# Walmart SE-III (Linux/C++) – Vizio Team | Walk-in Drive Interview Experience

Sharing my recent interview experience with **Walmart for an SE-III (Linux/C++) role with the Vizio team**.

### Walk-in Drive

I went to the Walmart office for what was advertised as a **walk-in drive**. However, after reaching the venue, HR informed me that it was actually a walk-in drive **only for shortlisted/selected candidates**.

The HR was kind enough to still arrange a first-round interview for me, which I appreciate.

### Technical Round 1

The first round was conducted by a **Tech Lead**.

The discussion started with questions about my current work and the projects I have been involved in. The interviewer then moved to:

* Linux / Linux OS
* C++
* Inter-Process Communication (IPC)
* Operating Systems concepts
* My current project's technical details
* Design Patterns
* Short LLD questions

I was able to answer the questions and explain my work and the concepts I had worked with.

### Hiring Manager Round

After the first round, I was asked to wait for the **Hiring Manager (HM) round**.

Interestingly, while other candidates appeared to be going through multiple technical rounds, I was directly moved to the HM round after lunch.

The HM primarily focused on understanding the **overall software product architecture of my current organization**, rather than going deep into the specific product/component I personally work on.

The discussion was quite fast-paced, with the interviewer asking questions continuously. I felt that there wasn't much opportunity to

I applied directly on the career portal. A recruiter called to say that my profile was shortlisted for interviews for Software Engineer III - (Java with DevOps). She said that there will be 3 rounds of interviews, 2 virtual and the last round F2F in Bangalore. The first round was scheduled 2 days after the initial call.

Began with an introduction and asked why my project used microservices architecture instead of a monolith. Asked me how much I would rate myself in DSA. I said 8/10. He said he would give a medium question, then proceeded to give a variation of LC 295. Find Median from Data Stream.

After conveying my approach, I was instructed to code in Java and explain the time complexities. I fumbled a little while explaining how a heap data structure works internally. Then the last 15 minutes were questions from my resume.

1. Which design pattern would you use to decide the object at runtime?
2. Active-active vs active-passive architecture.
3. How to make sure that Kafka publishes events in the same partition?
4. Redis - Distributed cache working.
5. What are Reentrant Locks? Can they work with different objects?
